tt_provider: Choose where the model runs. Local for offline work, cloud for hosted models.
tt_model: Choose which model to use. If the list is empty, refresh it or check the provider account.
tt_refresh: Reload the model list. Use after adding a new model or API key.
tt_rate_limit: Minimum pause between requests, in milliseconds. On a 429 the pack widens this by itself for a couple of minutes, honouring the provider's own Retry-After when it sends one.
tt_config: Settings received from the Loader node.
tt_image: Image or batch to analyze. Leave disconnected to generate from Prompt field.
tt_agent: Subject domain — what is in the frame.
tt_agent_focus: Craft layer to weigh heavier on top of the agent: composition, light, fine detail, cinematic read, or the subject's state and movement.
tt_custom_style: Custom style text. Overrides photo/art/nsfw preset styles.
tt_prompt:
WITHOUT AN IMAGE — the idea itself, expanded into a finished prompt:
  ginger cat on a windowsill, rain outside
  abandoned metro station, morning light through a hole in the ceiling

WITH AN IMAGE — what to focus on and what the text is for:
  emphasise the light and skin texture
  prompt for an album cover
  the cup on the table is the subject, not the person
  keep empty space on the right for a headline

WON'T WORK (this comes from the image):
  replace the woman with a man
  make her stand instead of sit
  remove the second person

Leave empty and the image is simply described in detail.
Details: docs/scanner-prompts.md
tt_neg_prompt:
Removes WORDS from the generated text, not objects from the image. Pose, subject and composition cannot be changed here — use the prompt field.

PUT HERE what the model adds on its own:
  cliches: masterpiece, best quality, 8k, highly detailed
  effects: bokeh, lens flare, dramatic vignette
  junk: watermark, logo, signature, text overlay
  defects: extra fingers, plastic skin, waxy texture
  judgements: beautiful, stunning, breathtaking

Short nouns, comma-separated, 5-10 of them. Not sentences with 'no': under FLUX / Z-Image Turbo / Krea 2 / Ideogram 4 / Video the list is flipped into positive wording, and 'do not make it blurry' has nothing to flip — write blurry.

Not sure what to put? Leave it empty, run once, and pick out the words that bother you in the answer.

tt_lang: Language of the answer. Auto replies in the language of your prompt.
tt_detail: How detailed the answer should be.
tt_model_type: Target generation model — adjusts prompt syntax, length, and format. Video is a universal profile for video models (MiniMax H2/H3, Wan, HunyuanVideo, LTX Video, Kling); MiniMax H3 gets a dedicated timeline shot-block profile.
tt_prompt_mode: Auto picks Hybrid or Two-Stage depending on whether a style is selected.
tt_photo_style: Photographic style overlay applied on top of the base description.
tt_nsfw_photo_style: Adult-only photographic style overlay (alternative to Photo style).
tt_art_style: Art style overlay applied on top of the base description.
tt_nsfw_art_style: Adult-only art style overlay (alternative to Art style).
tt_unload_llm: Local servers only (Ollama, LM Studio): unload the model from memory right after the prompt is generated, freeing VRAM for the image generation.
tt_temperature: Sampling temperature — higher is more creative, lower is more deterministic.
tt_max_tokens: Maximum tokens in the LLM response.
tt_provider_max_tokens: Maximum tokens in the response. 0 = provider default (no explicit limit).
tt_response_format: Output shape: prose text, flat comma-separated tags, or a JSON object.
tt_video_duration: Requested clip length in seconds. 0 = Auto (the LLM decides). The range follows the model: MiniMax H3 accepts 4-15 whole seconds (API limit), universal Video 2-20. Shown only for video model types.
tt_video_aspect: Aspect ratio written into the shot framing — for MiniMax H3 into the timeline header line ('10s, 16:9.'). Auto leaves the choice to the LLM. Shown only for video model types.
tt_video_sound: Sound design mode. Auto = the LLM decides; Off = silent clip (no sound clause); Layered = mandatory ambience + foley + music clause for audio-capable models (H3, Veo). Shown only for video model types.
tt_video_camera: Preferred camera move. The LLM builds the shot around it and may adapt per story stage — a preference, not a hard lock. Shown only for video model types.
tt_width: Target image width in pixels. Helps tailor prompt composition to aspect ratio if > 0.
tt_height: Target image height in pixels. Helps tailor prompt composition to aspect ratio if > 0.
tt_channel_value: Anything to broadcast: Model, VAE, Image, Latent, String, Int...
channel_panel_empty: Plug something in — every wired input becomes its own channel.
channel_targets_none: Nothing in the graph has a free input of this type.
channel_target_takeover: Replace the real wire with this channel
channel_cluster_hint: Several inputs of one type on this node. Pick a channel for each — nothing is connected until you confirm.
channel_ask_hint: Name it once — the answer is saved in the workflow and decides which sampler input the channel feeds.
channel_search_no_match: No matching nodes found for this filter.
wireless_diag_no_channels: No 📡 Channel nodes in this graph yet.
wireless_diag_dormant: {node} — input "{input}" is subscribed to {channel}, but a real wire already feeds it
wireless_diag_ambiguous: {node} — input "{input}" ({type}) could take {candidates}, so it takes none: pick one on the transmitter
wireless_diag_type_mismatch: {node} — input "{input}" is subscribed to {channel} ({channelType}), but the input is {inputType}
wireless_diag_unknown_channel: {node} — input "{input}" is subscribed to "{channel}", which does not exist
wireless_diag_self_loop: {node} — input "{input}" is subscribed to {channel}, which this node itself feeds
wireless_diag_unused_channel: {channel} — nothing in the graph is receiving it
tt_switch_input: Any incoming data signal (Image, Latent, Model, String, etc.).
tt_switch_enable: ON (True) passes the input signal through. OFF (False) sends `None` downstream, and the rest of the graph keeps running.
err_switch_no_input: 🔀 Cyber Switch is ON but nothing arrived on `input` — connect a signal to it. Everything downstream was skipped.
tt_max_image_side: Images are downscaled so their longest side does not exceed this value.
tt_provider_seed: Provider-side generation seed, if supported. -1 lets the provider pick one.
scn_seed_auto_random: Auto-random — a new seed is generated each run
scn_seed_mode_tt: Random generates a new seed each run.
scn_seed_use_last_tt: Reuse the seed from the last executed run.
scn_seed_new_fixed_tt: Generate a new random fixed seed.
scn_field_linked: 🔗 Text comes from the connected node
fld_linked_tt: Driven by the connected input — disconnect it to edit here.
scn_field_linked_tt: Driven by the connected input — disconnect it to type here.
sd_mode: Random generates a new seed each run.
sd_use_last: Reuse the seed from the last executed run.
sd_new_fixed: Generate a new random fixed seed.
utc_image: Input image to analyze. Optional if latent is connected instead — at least one of image/latent is required; source dimensions come from whichever is connected.
utc_upscale_model: Optional ESRGAN-style model. When connected, the image output is actually upscaled through it (then resized to the tile-aligned target). When left unconnected, image is passed through unchanged and this node is calculator-only.
upl_image: Input image to upscale. Optional if latent is connected instead — at least one of image/latent is required.
upl_model: ESRGAN-style upscale model. Only applies when image is connected — has no effect in latent-only mode.
utc_tile_size: Base tile size in pixels for tiled upscale.
utc_overlap: Tile overlap in pixels. Higher = fewer seams, more VRAM.
utc_latent: Optional latent to resize/tile alongside (or instead of) the image. When connected, the latent output is resized (bislerp) to the tile-aligned target and latent_tiles gets one crop per tile. Can stand in for image entirely — at least one of image/latent is required.
utc_auto_overlap: Ignore tile_overlap and derive it automatically from the tile size (~12.5%, min 32px) instead — keeps overlap proportional when you change tile_size. No effect when Full Auto is on (it already derives its own overlap).
utc_auto_mode: Full Auto: automatically choose tile settings based on profile.
utc_manual_cols: Force this many tile columns. 0 = compute from tile size.
utc_manual_rows: Force this many tile rows. 0 = compute from tile size.
utc_non_square: Enable non-square tiles with aspect-ratio awareness.
utc_auto_fix_edges: In Manual Tiles mode, shrink tile_size to the next standard size (1536/1024/768 → 512) instead of just warning when the grid would leave a thin edge tile. At 512 (smallest standard) it can't shrink further — the thin edge is then handled downstream by overlap/mask_blur. Does not affect an explicit manual column/row grid.
ks_eta: Noise multiplier for ancestral/SDE samplers (1.0 = standard, 0.0 = deterministic).
ks_bongmath: Enable bongmath implicit correction for RES4LYF samplers (ignored by standard samplers).
ks_preview: How the live sampling preview is rendered.
ks_vae_decode: Decode the result to an IMAGE preview/output. Needs a VAE.
ks_vae: VAE for decoding the preview/output image.
ks_script: Optional FiL HighRes-fix script to run after sampling.
hrf_upscale_type: Upscale in latent space, pixel space, or both.
hrf_ckpt: Checkpoint for the hires pass. '(use same)' reuses the base model.
hrf_same_seed: Reuse the sampler's seed for the hires pass.
hrf_denoise: Denoise strength for the hires re-sample.
hrf_iterations: How many upscale+resample passes to run.
hrf_total_scale_tt: Total cumulative upscale ratio across passes
hrf_cn_preproc: Preprocess the ControlNet hint image. 'none' feeds the raw upscaled image (right for tile ControlNets).
hrf_seed_auto_random: Auto-random — a new hires seed is generated each run
hrf_seed_mode_tt: Random generates a new hires seed each run.
hrf_seed_use_last_tt: Reuse the hires seed from the last executed run.
hrf_seed_use_last_prefix: Reuse the last run's hires seed:
hrf_seed_new_fixed_tt: Generate a new random fixed hires seed.
hrf_use_cn: Guide the hires pass with a ControlNet. Tile ControlNets work without a preprocessor.
hrf_script: Optional upstream FiL script to extend.
nsc_rng_source: Device the initial noise is drawn on. 'gpu' can better match Automatic1111-style noise for the same seed.
nsc_add_seed_noise: Blend in noise from a second seed for a controlled variation.
nsc_seed: Variation seed (used when Variation is ON).
nsc_weight: Variation strength: 0 = base seed only, 1 = variation seed only.
nsc_script: Optional upstream FiL script to extend.
tla_tiles: Batch of processed tile images — same order/count as the `tiles` output that produced `layout`.
tla_layout: Tile layout from FiL Upscaler Advanced/Simple's `layout` output.
tt_cw_method: Correction algorithm. Full Auto = Gray World white balance + LAB contrast enhancement.
tt_cw_strength: Overall correction strength. 0 = no change, 1 = full correction.
tt_cw_saturate: Percentile saturation for Channel Stretch (only used by that method).
tt_cw_preserve_skin: Preserve skin tones — prevents white balance from grey-washing faces.
tt_cw_reference: Reference image whose colour distribution to match.
tt_cw_wb_mask: Mask of a neutral-grey area to sample for white balance.
sm_base_prompt_ph: The prompt the styles are mixed onto…
sm_base_prompt_tt: Base prompt to apply style mixing onto.
sm_fusion_tt: Fast Stack just weights the descriptions. Smart Fusion asks the Vision LLM to synthesize one prompt.
cr_mode_tt: Original Shot builds a new frame around the scene. Reshoot locks a reference image and only changes the camera treatment.
cr_setup_mode_tt: Director Preset mode uses signature director visual styles and neutralizes manual hardware controls. Custom Hardware mode enables full manual control of all camera, lens, focal, aperture, and optics controls.
crp_scene_placeholder: What is happening in the frame…
cr_scene_tt: What the rig wraps. The camera treatment never touches it.
cr_scene_reshoot_tt: Reshoot reads the scene from the reference image — this text is ignored.
cr_camera_tt: Camera body. Film bodies wrap the shot in analog stock language, digital in sensor language.
cr_lens_tt: Lens glass — spherical or anamorphic optical character.
cr_focal_tt: Focal length, from ultra-wide environmental pressure to telephoto compression.
cr_aperture_tt: Aperture stop — how much of the frame holds focus.
cr_angle_tt: Camera angle and elevation relative to the subject.
cr_optics_tt: Lens filter, flares, or film grain texture.
cr_grade_on_tt: Apply a finish over the frame. Off keeps the rig to hardware and medium only.
cr_grade_tt: The color grade / finish applied over the frame.
cr_polish_tt: Deterministic is pure string assembly. LLM Polish rewrites the rig into fluent prose through the provider model.
ds_image: Images to turn into a dataset. The whole batch is processed, one file per frame.
ds_config: Provider Loader config. Required for LLM captioning — leave unconnected when captions come from the captions input or caption_mode is 'none'.
ds_captions: Manual captions, one per image, separated by a line containing only '---'. Accepts Optic Scanner output as-is. When filled, no LLM call is made.
ds_name: Dataset folder name under ComfyUI/output/datasets. Sanitized to a safe path segment.
ds_trigger: Unique token that activates the LoRA, prepended to every caption (e.g. 'ohwx'). Leave empty for a style LoRA.
ds_class: Class the subject belongs to (e.g. 'woman', 'car'). Follows the trigger word in captions and in the kohya folder name.
ds_resolution: Training resolution. Buckets are built around this area — 1024 for SDXL/Flux, 512-768 for SD 1.5.
ds_layout: kohya: <name>/img/<repeats>_<trigger> <class>/ plus dataset.toml. flat: images and captions directly in <name>/.
ds_repeats: Repeats per image per epoch — encoded in the kohya folder name and dataset.toml. Fewer images means more repeats.
ds_caption_mode: natural: prose for Flux/SDXL. tags: comma tags for SD 1.5/Pony. hybrid: short comma phrases. none: trigger word only, no LLM call.
ds_crop_mode: How the frame is cropped into its bucket. entropy keeps the most detailed region instead of the middle.
ds_dry_run: Compute buckets, captions and file names but write nothing. Read the report to check the plan first.
ds_write_mode: append: keep existing files and continue numbering. overwrite: delete this node's image/caption pairs in the folder first (other files are left alone).
ds_caption_words: Hard word limit per caption. Captions longer than this are truncated.
ds_caption_lang: Caption language. Trainers expect English unless the base model was trained otherwise.
ds_dont_caption: Invariants the captions must never mention (e.g. 'her face, red hair'). These belong to the trigger word — describing them stops the LoRA from learning them.
ds_caption_instruction: Extra instruction appended to every caption request.
ds_bucket_step: Bucket side divisor. 64 is the kohya default and fits SD/SDXL/Flux latents.
ds_caption_ext: Extension of the caption sidecar files. kohya defaults to .txt.
ds_image_format: png keeps the crop lossless; jpg saves disk space on large sets.
ds_jpg_quality: JPEG quality when image_format is jpg. Below ~90 the artifacts start training too.
ds_seed: Provider-side caption seed. -1 lets the provider pick one; a fixed value makes captions reproducible.
dsp_hint_no_config: ⚠️ Connect 🔌 Provider Loader to caption — or fill in captions below
dsp_ph_manual_captions: One per image, separated by a line with ---. Skips the LLM when filled.
dsp_ph_dont_caption: her face, red hair — belongs to the trigger word
tla_info: Feathers processed tiles back into one image.
ksp_after_generate_tt: What ComfyUI does to the seed once the prompt has run.
ksp_eta_ignored_tt: This sampler ignores eta — only ancestral/SDE samplers use it.
ksp_bongmath_ignored_tt: This sampler does not read the bongmath toggle.
nscp_after_generate_tt: What ComfyUI does to the variation seed once the prompt has run.
idcp_prompt_tt: Optional text to decompose. Ignored when an image is connected.
idcp_prompt_placeholder: Describe the scene, or wire an image instead…
idcp_needs_input: Connect an image or type a prompt — the node needs one of the two.
idcp_language_tt: Language of the decomposed Subject / Lighting / Composition / Style outputs.
fb_view_list_tt: A dense list — easier once there are hundreds
fb_view_grid_tt: Picture tiles, for browsing by eye
fb_grip_side: Drag to resize. Double-click to reset.
fb_grip_detail: Drag to resize. Double-click to reset.
pmp_search_tt: Ranks by how well the name matches, best first
pmp_pick_to_see: Pick a model to see what it is.
sb_search_tt: Searches all four lists at once, by name and by category
sb_pick_to_see: Click a style to add it and see it bigger.
sb_clear_all_tt: Remove every selected style from all four lists
pm_no_key_hint: No API key for this provider yet.
pm_key_file_hint: Key saved in data/auth.json — Delete removes it.
tt_cycler_source_mode: Model source: Checkpoints, Diffusion Models (UNet), or Connected Signals.
tt_cycler_model_list: Multiline list of model filenames. If empty, auto-scans all installed models in folder.
tt_cycler_filter_pattern: Wildcard pattern to filter models (e.g. *flux* or sdxl*).
tt_cycler_cycle_mode: Iteration order: Sequential (Loop), Sequential (Stop), Ping-Pong, Random, or Fixed Index.
tt_cycler_index: Starting 0-based model index (auto-advances per run when Auto Next is ON).
tt_cycler_auto_advance: Automatically switch to next model after each generation run.
tt_cycler_unload_previous: Unload previous model from GPU memory before loading next model to prevent OOM.
tt_cycler_free_vram: Flush PyTorch CUDA memory cache between model switches.
tt_cycler_skip_on_error: Skip corrupt or missing model files and proceed to next model without crashing queue.
tt_cycler_weight_dtype: Weight precision for UNet/Diffusion models (default, fp16, bf16, fp8_e4m3fn).
tt_cycler_clip_in: Passthrough or fallback CLIP for UNet models.
tt_cycler_vae_in: Passthrough or fallback VAE for UNet models.
tt_cycler_model_slot: Select specific model. Selecting a model activates the next slot.
cycler_runs_hint: Queue runs one model per run — press Run All to queue the whole cycle at once.
cycler_runs_hint_empty: No models in the cycle yet — add rows, or Populate Folder.
tt_lora_loader_model: Input diffusion MODEL to apply the active LoRA adapter to.
tt_lora_loader_clip: Input CLIP encoder to apply the active LoRA adapter to.
tt_lora_loader_lora_list: List of LoRA filenames to cycle through (one per line). Supports inline weights: 'my_lora.safetensors:0.8:0.5'.
tt_lora_loader_filter_pattern: Wildcard (e.g. '*cyberpunk*'). Left empty the whole stack runs; set, only stack entries matching it are applied.
tt_lora_loader_strength_model: Default MODEL strength (overridden by inline weight if provided).
tt_lora_loader_strength_clip: Default CLIP strength (overridden by inline weight if provided).
tt_lora_loader_skip_on_error: If a LoRA file fails to load, log warning and skip to next LoRA instead of crashing queue.
err_lora_no_input: 🧬 LoRA Loader: nothing is wired in — connect MODEL (and CLIP if the LoRA touches it).
ee_clip: Text encoder of the edit model (e.g. Qwen3-VL for FLUX.2/Krea2).
ee_prompt: Edit instruction: what to change, keep, or compose from the references.
ee_vae: VAE of the edit model. Only needed when reference_mode uses latents.
ee_images: Reference images to edit from. Each adds its latent to the conditioning — VRAM and sampling time grow with every one.
ee_method: Only used when reference_mode sends latents. On Krea 2 every value behaves the same except index_timestep_zero.
ee_out: Prompt conditioning carrying every reference latent — feed the sampler's positive input.
eep_prompt_ph: What to change, keep, or compose from the references…
eep_refs_tt: Reference images wired into the slots below the panel — each one adds a latent to the conditioning.
ee_mode: How references reach the model. 'vision': the text encoder looks at them, nothing enters the frame (Krea 2). 'latents': VAE-encoded into the frame itself (FLUX.2/Kontext) — this is what tiles the source into the output. 'both': both channels.
ee_system: Your own role text. Used whenever system_preset is 'none' and this field is not empty.
ee_preset: Role sent to the text encoder. 'none' for a prompt that gives an instruction ('change X, keep Y') — it is followed most closely that way. 'use reference' for a prompt that only describes a style, which otherwise leaves the model no reason to look at the reference. On 'none' the system_prompt field below supplies a role of your own, if you type one.
ee_prompt_preset: A ready-made opening, prepended to whatever you type. Edit models follow an explicit instruction far more closely than a bare description.
ee_strength: How hard the references pull on the text encoder. 1.0 is the plain encode and costs nothing; anything else encodes a second time against blank references and interpolates, so 0 ignores them and above 1 exaggerates them. No effect in reference_mode 'latents'.
ee_vl_mp: Size of the copy the text encoder reads. 0.15 MP (~384x384) is what core uses.
ee_lat_mp: Cap for the copy the VAE encodes, when reference_mode uses latents.
ee_summary: What this run did with the references, and a note when a setting looks like a bug but is not.
